chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, that he said:
“I would not carry out a hadd punishment upon a man in the land of the enemy until he leaves it, for fear that zeal might carry him away and he would join the enemy.”

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْعَدُوِّ: the territory or land of the enemy
key_terms.فَيَلْحَقَ بِالْعَدُوِّ: so that he may join or defect to the enemy

ai.seo_question: Why should a hadd punishment not be carried out in enemy territory according to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling attributed to 'Ali عليه السلام that a hadd punishment should not be carried out in enemy territory. The reason given is the concern that tribal zeal or indignation may drive the punished person to defect to the enemy, showing consideration of broader harm in applying punishment.
